title: A state schema's collection field carries two exclamation marks for two different reasons, and the outer one is what guarantees an empty list rather than null
content:
The state schema is GraphQL SDL, and the one piece of syntax that carries real semantics for a document model is the double `!` on a collection:

```graphql
type TodoListState {
  items: [TodoItem!]!
}

type TodoItem {
  id: OID!
  text: String!
  checked: Boolean!
}
```

- the **inner** `!` on `TodoItem!` means no entry inside the list may be null;
- the **outer** `!` on `[TodoItem!]!` means the list itself may not be null — "it can be an empty list `[]`, but it cannot be absent".

That is why the vault's own document-modelling rule holds that collections should always be `[Type!]!`: the outer `!` is what lets a document be created empty without the field being `null`, and the inner `!` is what stops a hole appearing inside it.

The other Powerhouse-specific piece is the **`OID`** scalar — a custom scalar for unique identifiers in document models, with automatic ID generation when used with `generateId()` from the document-model core library. Its purpose in the example is stated plainly: `id: OID!` is "crucial for referencing specific items, for example when updating or deleting them" — an operation input has to name the row it changes.

Beyond the built-in scalars (`String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Boolean`, `ID`), the Document-Engineering system adds custom scalars **linked to reusable front-end components**, which is what makes a scalar choice a UI decision as well as a data one.
